epic.intent:
# Outcome

Agents that belong to an epic are handled inside the epic screen. The View group gets a fourth button, right after List: **Agent**, in bold, with a small person icon. It swaps the stage from the graph, list or scorecard to the epic's agents. Each agent shows as a GUI chat: bubbles, streamed text, tool cards, subagent threads, docked approval and question cards, a composer with Stop. The GUI is powered by the agent's CLI on the backend, the way Ada (onebrief-harness `packages/desktop`) drives OMP over `--mode rpc`. Folder and project-less chats outside an epic also open as a GUI by default, and each chat can be toggled to its terminal and back.

## User journeys
1. **Watch and steer a run.** The person opens an epic with an active run and clicks **Agent**. The orchestrator is selected and streams its work live. Worker subagents appear as their own entries. The person types to the orchestrator, or to a worker; worker messages are relayed through the orchestrator. If an approval or question comes up, a card docks above the composer.
2. **Plan with an agent.** On an epic with no agents, the Agent tab offers **Start planner**. That starts a planner chat bound to the epic, which appears in the list from then on.
3. **Ordinary chats.** New chat opens a GUI chat with Skitarii when it is installed and signed in, otherwise with whichever GUI-capable agent is signed in (Claude). **Terminal** switches an idle chat to its TUI on the same session; **GUI** switches back.

## Standards
Only the project's Definition of Done gates acceptance (lint, typecheck, test, coverage, deadcode, build), once at the sprint acceptance. Tests-first and Fireguard are **not** required. Every ticket writes and runs the tests in its **Tests** section and its targeted checks only. Flakes and timeouts are failures; never rerun to green.

**Unattended verification is a requirement.** Every acceptance criterion must be checkable by an agent:
- unit and jsdom tests;
- a deterministic fake agent CLI (no network, no sign-in);
- `node scripts/capture-agent-chat.mjs`: screenshots and DOM observations of each Agent tab state, which the reviewer opens and inspects;
- `node scripts/e2e-agent-chat.mjs`: the built app driven over CDP with the fake CLI.

Both scripts use the repo's own Electron, so they need no external browser.

**Execution host:** this epic runs on a **Windows** machine with a full install of the app, where the screenshots and e2e run directly. Code, scripts and tests must be Windows-first and POSIX-safe. Inside this Mac session's sandbox Chromium and Electron cannot start, so the planning host is not the execution host.

# Design

## 1. Modules
- **Main**, new folder `src/main/agentChat/`:
  - `claudeProtocol.ts` and `ompProtocol.ts`: pure translators and encoders.
  - `agentChatLaunch.ts`: pure argv, env and cwd.
  - `agentProcess.ts`: JSONL child-process runner.
  - `agentChatSessions.ts`: lifecycle, grants and persistence.
  - `pendingPrompts.ts`.
  - `agentChatIpc.ts`.
  - `__fixtures__/`: golden transcripts and `fakeAgentCli.mjs`.
- **Shared:** `src/shared/agents/pickChatAgent.ts` and `src/shared/agents/agentChat.ts`, holding the channels, schemas, `AgentChatEvent`, `PendingPrompt`, `AgentChatSnapshot` and `AgentChatApi`. `ChatRecord` gains optional `epicId` and `surface`.
- **Renderer:**
  - new `src/renderer/src/agentChat/`: model, hook, `AgentChat`, `StreamingBubble`, `PendingPromptCard`;
  - `src/renderer/src/epic/EpicAgentPanel.tsx` and `epicAgentsView.ts`;
  - the Agent button in `epic/WorkspaceHeader.tsx`, with `layout: 'agent'` in `epic/workspaceState.ts`.

## 2. Transport
Each GUI chat runs one CLI child process with piped stdio, speaking JSONL in both directions. There is no vendor SDK and no per-vendor adapter layer; each CLI's own structured mode is used.
- **Skitarii / omp:** `omp --mode rpc-ui …`. `rpc-ui` is required for OMP's ask tool. This is the default when it is installed and signed in.
- **Claude:** `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio --append-system-prompt-file … [--settings …] (--session-id|--resume) <uuid>`. It is never run with `--bare`, `--no-session-persistence` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
- **Other kinds** (codex, cursor, autonomous, custom) have no verified structured mode, so they keep the terminal.

## 3. Data model
The translators turn CLI lines into the **existing** `ChatItem` kinds:
- `user_message`, `assistant_text`, `tool_call`, `thread`, `approval_request`, `approval_decision`, `error` and `turn_stopped` are persisted to `<chatId>.jsonl` and rendered by the existing `ChatTranscript`, `ToolCallRow` and `ThreadBlock`;
- ephemeral `delta` events carry streamed text;
- `status`, `pending` and `queued` events carry state.

Raw CLI lines never cross IPC.

## 4. Approvals and questions
Claude `can_use_tool` (AskUserQuestion becomes a question; every other tool becomes an approval) and OMP blocking `extension_ui_request`s become a `PendingPrompt`. Main holds it, replays it on attach, and never auto-answers it.
- "Allow for this chat" is offered only when the CLI suggests permissions, and the CLI applies it (`updatedPermissions`).
- AskUserQuestion is never auto-denied.
- The memory-guard hook stays, through the identical `--settings` file. Whether it reaches the host in `-p` mode is observed in `proto`, or documented as unverified.

## 5. Surface
`surface: 'gui' | 'terminal'` lives on the chat record.
- New chats take it from `pickChatAgent`; legacy chats are terminal.
- A toggle is allowed only when the chat is idle. It stops the live owner, revokes its grant, and resumes the same session id in the other owner.
- One owner per chat: each owner refuses to start while the other is live.

## 6. Epic binding
`epicId` is stored when orchestrator, transfer, conversation and planner chats are created. Legacy bindings (`runId` of the epic's run, `transferEpicId`, `conversation.epicId`) are still honoured. Worker agents are the orchestrator's subagent threads. Messaging a worker sends the orchestrator a fixed marker message, `[Message from the person for your worker subagent, thread <id>]`, which is defined in the role guides. Workers answer to the orchestrator, and the model-written thread label is never interpolated into the message.

## 7. Security rules (as for terminal chats, except Claude's trust dialog; see the last bullet)
- The renderer never supplies the executable, args, cwd or env.
- Chats are pinned to the folder's canonical path.
- `DM_SESSION_TOKEN` is env-only; grants are renewed hourly and revoked on every exit.
- `maskAgentChatSecretsDeep` (claim tokens **and** `dmg_` grant tokens) runs on every stored or pushed string, including status details and stderr tails. `maskClaimTokensDeep` alone does not cover the grant token.
- The composer is text-only in v1 (at most 20,000 characters); no bytes or paths cross IPC.
- Every handler goes through `guardIpc` with strict zod input.
- Quit is held until the agent processes have exited (5 s bound).
- There is no idle stop.
- Claude `-p` skips its workspace trust dialog, so tracking a folder in Dark Mechanicus is the trust decision. The docs state this.

## 8. Ada
Ada is read for ideas only (pure reducer, docked approval card, stream throttle, fake CLI with e2e). Its code is not copied, because it lives in a private company repository.

# Sprints
1. **Base GUI**, which everything else builds on:
   - GUI chats, the Agent tab and the terminal toggle;
   - the right rail with the named agent tree, live To-dos, the Changes card and the activity line;
   - named approvals, the Magos arbiter, OS notifications and Notifications & approvals settings;
   - restart resume after an app update.
2. **Delivered sprint transition.** Dark Mechanicus gains a structured per-sprint `delivery {target, release, verifyInstalled}` gate. After a delivering sprint's checkpoint, the next sprint's claims wait until the server verifies three things: the increment is on the target branch, a release contains it, and the installed app runs that release or later. The person can waive it. Plans saved before the field existed keep their exact hash.
3. **Screenshots and the agent browser:**
   - images in GUI chats, crossing IPC by id only;
   - agent image results shown inline, which can become ticket evidence;
   - an in-app browser in the rail's Browser tab, driven by agents through narrow grant-gated `dm browser_*` commands, with origin approval by the person, Stop, Take control and Hand back.
4. **Desktop control in GUI chats.** The merged Windows Skitarii desktop-control feature (epic `ep_01m794777kq96v22ryvxv5pdye`) is mounted into Skitarii GUI chats: header menu, rail card, tree lock and inline screenshots. Nothing is reimplemented. The sprint is gated on that epic being merged and delivered.

Each sprint ends at a human checkpoint. After approval, the Magos delivers the increment to `main` by pull request, the Deploy workflow releases it, the person presses Restart now on the Windows host, and the next sprint opens with a delivery-check ticket.

# Design, continued
## 9. Right rail, agent tree and callsigns
- **The rail:** a fixed 280 px right rail that collapses to a 40 px strip showing counts. Its Agents tab holds the tree and the Changes card. Browser and Files tab slots are reserved.
- **The tree:** generic, nested and named. It is reused in ordinary GUI chats as a toggleable rail.
- **Callsigns:** Magos (Start-run orchestrator chat records only), Lexmechanic (planner records), `Acolyte:<KEY>` (worker), `Inquisitor:<KEY>` (adversarial reviewer), `Servitor:<KEY>`/`Servitor-<n>` (other helpers).
  - Main resolves callsigns once and stamps them on thread items, approval requests and prompts.
  - Labels come from the Magos's `<Role>:<KEY> <purpose>` subagent descriptions, parsed by a strict whitelist.
  - The claim-token binding (the `at_` id read from the raw spawn prompt before masking, storing only `{threadId → attemptId}`) wins over the label.
  - Claude GUI launches add `--forward-subagent-text`.

## 10. To-dos, Changes and activity
- **To-dos:** an ephemeral per-thread `todos` event plus a snapshot field, fed by Claude TodoWrite or TaskCreate/TaskUpdate and by OMP `todo` phases, `get_state` and `todo_auto_clear`. The card is Ada-style: collapsible, at most ~5 rows, with the lingering rule. Successful todo calls are hidden from the transcript; failed ones stay visible.
- **Changes:** built from file-tool paths, kept verbatim and masked. It opens Source control at the file.
- **Activity line:** uses the injectable clock and warns after 30 s of silence.

## 11. Magos arbiter and notifications
- **Why an arbiter:** while a worker's tool approval is pending, the Magos's own turn is blocked, so the live Magos cannot answer it.
- **How it works:** main spawns a short-lived, tool-less, grant-less, non-persistent arbiter session of the same agent kind, in an empty temp folder. The session sees the masked prompt, the requester's callsign and ticket, the epic Standards and the person's auto-handle notes, and must return strict JSON: `allow_once`, `deny` or `escalate`.
- **What escalates:** a 60 s bound, invalid output, a timeout or an error.
- **Never arbitrated:**
  - questions;
  - prompts outside Start-run orchestrator chats;
  - paths outside the folder;
  - the person's always-ask list;
  - browser site approvals (S3);
  - desktop-control prompts (S4).
- **Records:** decisions are stored as `approval_decision` with `decidedBy: 'magos'` and the reason. A person's answer always wins.
- **Notifications:** escalations, questions, checkpoint-ready, run failed and run stalled raise OS notifications (by default only when the window is unfocused). Clicking one lands on the card.
- **Settings:** stored in main. Loosening a security setting requires a native confirmation.

successCriteria.text: In any epic the View group reads Graph, List, **Agent** (bold, person icon), Scorecard; the Agent tab shows the selected agent's GUI chat with a right-rail nested agent tree using Mechanicus callsigns (Magos, Acolyte:DM-n, Inquisitor:DM-n, Servitor, Lexmechanic)

Chats render as GUIs (bubbles, streamed text, tool cards, threads, live To-dos, Changes, activity line, docked named approval and question cards) over Skitarii `omp --mode rpc-ui` or the signed-in Claude stream-json; every chat toggles to its terminal on the same session
Worker approvals are first decided by the Magos arbiter or escalated; the person gets needs-you badges and OS notifications governed by in-app Notifications & approvals settings

Sprints can declare a structured Delivered transition (merged to the target branch, released, installed app updated) that holds the next sprint until verified or waived, without changing older plan hashes; each sprint of this epic is delivered to main and verified on the Windows host before the next starts
Agents and the person exchange screenshots in GUI chats by id only, and agents drive an in-app browser in the rail through grant-gated dm commands with person-approved origins, Stop and Take control

On Windows, Skitarii GUI chats host the merged desktop-control feature (menu, rail card, tree lock, inline screenshots) without reimplementing its consent logic, and the arbiter never decides desktop prompts

Security rules hold throughout (no renderer-chosen exe/args/cwd/env, env-only grants, claim and grant tokens masked, quit waits for agents), and every sprint is verified unattended on the Windows host with tests, fake-CLI e2e and inspected screenshots, plus the full Definition of Done at each acceptance

bundle.rationale:
# Plan rationale

## Evidence inspected (base commit 3e5597a4, 2026-11-20)
A six-agent research swarm read these areas, and the planner checked the key facts directly:
- the epic screen;
- the chat backend;
- Ada's desktop app;
- project history;
- CLI protocols;
- verification tooling.

Key facts:
- **Epic view.** The view switcher is `ViewToggle`, built from `aria-pressed` buttons in a `role=group` labelled "View" (`epic/WorkspaceHeader.tsx:11-39`). `layout` is `'graph'|'list'`, plus a separate `scorecardOpen` flag (`epic/workspaceState.ts`). There is no person icon in `components/Icon.tsx`.
- **Chats today.** Chats are PTY terminals (`src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts`). Transcripts live in JSONL `ChatItem` files that nothing writes any more (`src/main/agents/chatStore.ts`).
- **No epic link.** `ChatRecord` has no `epicId`; orchestrator chats store only `runId`.
- **Previous GUI chat.** The earlier GUI chat (sessionManager plus adapters over the Claude Agent SDK, Codex app-server and ACP) was removed in 87102b0c (the "Terminal chats" epic), at the person's 2026-10-30 direction: "protocol adapters … make chats inflexible" (`docs/design/chat-shells.md:5,217`).
- **Ada.** Ada drives `ada omp --mode rpc` (OMP's RPC JSONL) from `pi-rpc-manager.ts`, with a pure reducer, a docked approval card and a fake CLI with e2e tests.
- **Claude CLI.** Claude Code 2.1.329 is installed and has `-p`, `--input-format/--output-format stream-json`, `--include-partial-messages`, `--permission-prompts` and `--resume`. The old SDK spawned the CLI with `--permission-prompt-tool stdio`. `--bare` is rejected here by managed settings (forceLoginOrgUUID).
- **Other CLIs.** `omp`, `codex` and `cursor` are not installed on this Mac. The OMP RPC protocol is known from Ada's types and `docs/reports/omp-cli.md`.
- **Screenshots.** There is no screenshot dependency. Preview pages (`preview/inbox`) mount real components over the renderer fakes. Headless Chromium (`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1248`) crashes inside the session sandbox with `bootstrap_check_in … Permission denied (1100)`; the planner observed this directly.
- **Gate timing.** The full DoD gate takes about 3.5 minutes (DM-400 summary).

## Decisions from the person (2026-11-20)
- **CLI:** Skitarii (omp) is the default when installed, like Ada. Otherwise the GUI is powered by whichever agent is signed in.
- **Folder chats:** GUI by default everywhere, with a terminal toggle.
- **Agents:** every agent tied to an epic is listed and chattable.
- **Shape:** one sprint and one human approval. The epic must run fast with no human intervention, so every step must be agent-verifiable.
- **Host:** the epic will be transferred to a **Windows** machine with a full install of the app, where screenshots run. This replaced the option of excluding the capture scripts from the sandbox.

## Planner decisions, with reasons
1. **Structured CLI modes, not adapters.** This reverses part of the terminal-only decision, as the person directed. It still keeps that decision's core objection: there is no vendor SDK and no per-vendor adapter layer. Each CLI's own JSONL mode feeds a thin pure translator into the existing `ChatItem` model. The terminal stays one toggle away.
   - Rejected: restoring the old sessionManager and SDK adapters. That would bring back the SDK dependency and the inflexibility the person objected to.
2. **v1 covers Skitarii and Claude only.** Only these two CLIs have a documented structured mode. "Whichever agent is signed in" therefore resolves to: Skitarii, then Claude, then a terminal for other kinds. Codex `exec --json` cannot be verified here and is a follow-up.
3. **Reuse the existing `ChatItem` schema and transcript renderer** (ChatTranscript, ToolCallRow, ThreadBlock) instead of porting Ada's message model. This means less new UI and fewer coverage risks.
4. **Approvals in the GUI.** They use `--permission-prompt-tool stdio` (Claude) and `extension_ui_request` (OMP), held in main and never auto-answered.
   - Rejected: `--permission-prompts none`. It auto-denies, which is the same stall as lesson L11.
   - Rejected: bypass modes. They would lower the security posture.
5. **Workers are subagent threads.** In-process workers are not separate CLI sessions, so "chattable" for a worker means a message relayed by the orchestrator, sent with the fixed marker `[Message from the person for your worker subagent, thread <id>]`, which the role guides define. This matches the collaboration policy: workers answer only to the orchestrator.
6. **Keep the Agent button an `aria-pressed` button in the existing group.** Converting the group to an ARIA tablist would break about 6 test files' queries for no user-visible gain. The bold style is scoped to `.ew-toggle-agent`, because `.ew-toggle` is shared with BranchMenu and editorFields.
7. **`layout: 'agent'`** extends the layout union instead of adding another overlay flag, which would create precedence bugs with `scorecardOpen` and `checkpointOpen`.
8. **Verification without new dependencies, and Windows-first.** Screenshots use the repo's own Electron: a hidden `BrowserWindow` loads a Vite preview page, then calls `capturePage`. The e2e drives the built app over CDP with Node's global WebSocket, following the Windows-shaped `scripts/first-prompt-smoke.mjs`. The fake agent is seeded as a claude-kind agent through an npm-style `.cmd` shim, which `resolveClaudeExecutable` already follows.
   - Rejected: Playwright. It needs an install and a browser-version match.
   - Rejected: the cached chrome-headless-shell. It is a Mac-only path.
9. **One sprint.** The deliverable is a single coherent outcome, and the person asked for a single approval. Interface risk is held inside the sprint by `proto` (the first prerequisite) and by early row checks at the translator, session and IPC joins.
10. **Ada code is not copied.** It is a private company repository, so the ideas are reimplemented.

11. **Red-team pass (4 refuting agents, 58 findings, all applied before Save).** The findings that changed the plan:
    - `maskClaimTokensDeep` does not mask `dmg_` grant tokens. A new `maskAgentChatSecretsDeep` and a `[leak]` fake scenario now prove masking.
    - The fake CLI must answer `--version` and `auth status`, run a TUI mode, log pids and renumber ids per turn.
    - OMP needs `--mode rpc-ui`, `set_subagent_subscription`, `follow_up`/`queue_update`, `rpc_chunk` reassembly and every blocking extension-UI method.
    - Claude AskUserQuestion arrives through `can_use_tool`. `request_user_dialog` has no evidence, and "allow for this chat" encodes `updatedPermissions`.
    - Script tests must be `.test.mjs`.
    - The `DmApi` bridge moved into `contract`.
    - `sessions` and `e2e` were each split in two.
    - New edges `approvals→surface→ipc→routing` remove same-file collisions.
    - `surface` is set centrally by agent kind in `ChatRecords.createChat`.
    - Image attachments are cut from v1.
    - The worker relay uses a fixed marker defined in the role guides, and never interpolates model-written labels.
    - Covers no longer depend on pgrep or on deleted temp dirs.

12. **Second refuting pass (14 findings, all applied):** the Windows `.cmd` shim and running a `.js` shim target; spawning the fake on Windows via `process.execPath` or a shim; first-prompt delivery and start-on-open for GUI chats; LF-pinned fixtures; stripping `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`; OMP approval recognition and `set_ask_dialog`; testable `wireAgentChats`; the `SKILLS_VERSION` bump; `chats:read` with `live`; Windows signals and pid recycling; blank captures.

## Windows execution-host preflight (UNVERIFIED from the planning host; the orchestrator checks before the first claim)
In the repository root on the Windows host, in the worker's own shell:
1. `git rev-parse HEAD` shows base `3e5597a4` or a descendant on the epic branch `epic-agent-gui-chat`.
2. `node --version` (planning host: v24.19.0) and `npm --version` (11.17.0). The repo has no `engines` pin, so use the versions that built the last release on that host.
3. `node_modules` is present and matches `package-lock.json`. Do not run `npm ci` speculatively (`docs/runbooks/offline-development.md`); if it is missing, `npm ci` is the only allowed install (lockfile-pinned, project-local).
4. `cmd /c "set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=&& npx electron --version"` prints a version starting `v42.` (an inherited `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` would otherwise print Node's version). `npm run build` succeeds. Both capture and e2e depend on this.
5. `npx vitest run src/main/terminals/claudeExecutable.test.ts` passes. This proves the child-process and shim path that the fake agent relies on.
6. Optional, for the `proto` live probes only: `claude --version` and `omp --version`. Missing is fine and recorded; nothing is installed.

If 1-5 do not all pass, stop and report to the person; do not start tickets.

## Assumptions
- The golden fixtures from `proto` match the real CLIs closely enough. The translators skip unknown events rather than fail.
- The OMP path is proven against fixtures built from the Ada-derived fact sheet (embedded in `proto`) and the omp-cli report, which was recorded on the Windows host with omp 18.16.0. If omp is installed there, `proto` also captures its real ready frame. No live model turn gates acceptance.
- A live Claude turn is an optional observation in `proto`, never a gate.
- The Windows host can launch Electron unattended (it has a full app install). If it cannot, capture and e2e fail loudly, and the acceptance node reports visual proof as unmet; it never skips.

## Risks and mitigations
- **The CLI protocol drifts with Claude auto-updates.** Mitigations: tolerant translators, unknown events counted, and a golden-fixture test per scenario.
- **Two owners per chat** (GUI and PTY) could double-spawn or race grants. Mitigation: `isLive` mutual exclusion; the toggle runs only when idle; the old grant is revoked before the new one is issued.
- **Approval prompts deadlock an unattended run.** Mitigations: prompts are held and replayed on attach, never auto-denied, and block only their own chat, as the terminal does today.
- **Token leakage through stored transcripts.** Mitigations: masking in the translators and again on append; tests plant a token and grep for it.
- **Coverage thresholds** (97/95/96/97) fail late. Mitigation: pure view-model modules with unit tests in every ticket.
- **Quit hangs.** Mitigation: `busy`/`dispose` cover GUI processes, with process-group kill bounded at 5 s; the e2e asserts that no process survives.
- **Windows-specific breakage** (paths, CRLF, `.cmd` shims, process trees). Mitigations: Windows-first rules in every ticket body; `processTree`'s existing `taskkill /t /f`; e2e shims tested against `SHIM_TARGET`.
- **Unverified memory guard in `-p` mode.** Mitigations: an optional `proto` probe; otherwise the docs state the gap honestly.

## Non-goals
- Codex, Cursor, Autonomous or custom CLIs in GUI mode.
- Image attachments in GUI chats.
- A model picker.
- Auto-binding folder chats that created an epic. They bind only when started from the epic: Start planner, Start run, transfer or board message.
- Notifications.
- Cults.
- Reconciling the stale OMP epic record (it shows backlog although it shipped in 261f9669 and 4f56cc73).
- Changing the sprint-checkpoint approval, which stays human.

## Graph
- **Row 1:** proto, contract, tab.
- **Row 2:** fakecli, claudeparse, ompparse, launch, transcript, chatmodel.
- **Then:**
  - process;
  - sessions, which joins the translators, launch, process and transcript;
  - sessionsend → approvals → surface → ipc → routing, a serial chain because they share `agentChatSessions.ts`, `chatHandlers.ts` and `bootstrap.ts`;
  - in parallel: chatview → approvalcard and chatpane;
  - epicpanel, which joins tab, chatview and routing, then redirects;
  - capture, e2eharness (after ipc), e2e and docs.
- **Critical path:** proto → claudeparse/ompparse → sessions → sessionsend → approvals → surface → ipc → routing → epicpanel → redirects → e2e.
- **Row checks:** run scoped typecheck plus `npx vitest run src/main/agentChat` at the sessions join, and `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/epic src/renderer/src/agentChat` at the epicpanel join.
- **Verification exceptions** are declared in `e2e` (15-minute noninterruptible build-plus-run) and in `proto` (40-minute bounded investigation).

# Expansion (2026-11-20, third round of decisions)
## The person's decisions
- **Feature scope:** add the right-rail named agent tree, Ada-style live To-dos, ticket-named workers with Mechanicus callsigns, named approvals with needs-you badges and notifications (plus notification settings), the Changes card and the activity line.
- **Big three:** screenshots, the agent browser and desktop control go in **separate later sprints**, with the base GUI first. Between sprints, the increment must be merged and the update must have landed on the Windows install. The next sprint verifies that at its start.
- **The Delivered transition** is to be **built as a Dark Mechanicus feature in this epic** (Sprint 2).
- **Approvals:** "Magos sees and decides".
- **Callsigns:** Magos, Acolyte, Inquisitor, Lexmechanic and Servitor.
- **Sprint 4:** desktop control is kept, gated on the Windows desktop-control epic merging.

## Research
A five-scout feature swarm covered Ada's GUI, Codex, Claude Code (desktop, VS Code, web), Cursor/Antigravity/Cline/Copilot/Devin and others, plus feasibility in this repo. It produced a 17-item catalogue (scratch evidence, summarised here):
- None of these apps ships a nested, named agent tree; Ada's Tasks panel is flat.
- Ada's TodoPanel lingering rule and its hiding of todo calls are worth copying.
- The claim-token binding exists in `src/core/space/hostTranscripts.ts`.
- Electron 42.11.18 provides `WebContentsView`, `webContents.debugger` and `capturePage`.
- The browser is a new privileged subsystem: Ada needed about 1,900 lines.

Six parallel drafters then wrote the new tickets with verified source locations.

## Planner decisions (each recorded with its reason)
1. **The Magos arbiter.** It is a separate tool-less session, not the live Magos. While a worker's approval is pending, the Magos's turn is blocked inside the Task/subagent call, so a message to it would deadlock. The arbiter keeps the person's intent: a Magos decision, recorded as `decidedBy: magos`.
   - The arbiter decides approvals only, never questions, because its verdict schema cannot answer one.
   - It runs only for Start-run orchestrator chats (role orchestrator plus `runId`).
   - Site approvals (S3) and desktop-control prompts (S4) are never arbitrated. Network egress and OS-level control are treated as the person's call, and accessibility and page text are injection vectors. **Flagged to the person.**
   - It can never choose `allow_chat`.
2. **Callsigns are resolved once, in main**, and stamped on items, so the tree, cards, notifications and arbiter agree. The tree drafter's duplicate renderer-side parser and binding tickets were dropped in favour of the approvals drafter's main-side design.
3. **Restart resume moved from S2 into S1.** The S1→S2 update then already brings the Magos back with no person typing.
4. **This epic's own transitions use text criteria plus delivery-check tickets.** A plan holding the new `delivery` field can only be saved by a build that has S2. So S2, S3 and S4 open with manual delivery-check tickets, and this epic never declares the structured `delivery` field. **Forward-compat rule:** never save a plan with `delivery` until the S2 release is installed on every machine that opens the folder.
5. **Merging to main** happens by orchestrator pull request after each checkpoint. Normal branch protection applies, with no admin bypass. It is requested explicitly in each sprint's exit criteria, per `skills/knowledge/orchestrator/post-checkpoint-delivery.md`. The person still presses Restart now to install each update, because an agent restarting the app would kill its own process.
6. **The browser is enabled by default** behind fail-closed origins, with one agent tab per chat in S3. **Flagged to the person.**
7. **`s4-ompshim`** follows npm `.cmd` shims for omp on Windows, so a fake Skitarii can run unattended. It also changes how an npm-installed omp starts in the terminal (node.exe instead of cmd.exe), which is judged safe. **Flagged to the person.**

## Added risks
- **S1 grows to 63 tickets.** Mitigations: wide parallelism, serialized same-file chains and row checks at the arbiter and notifier joins.
- **Kernel word cap:** `skills/orchestrator.md` is at 773 of 800 words. New guidance goes into knowledge facts.
- **Arbiter prompt injection:** allow_once only, never-arbitrate rules, every decision recorded, and the person's toggle. The person accepted model-made allow decisions.
- **S4 depends on another in-progress epic.** If that epic is not merged when S3 ends, the run waits at the S3 checkpoint for the person.
- **Windows install paths for version checks are unverified from the planning host.** The delivery-check tickets record the real paths.

## Graph
- **S1:** the base chain (proto → translators → sessions → sessionsend → approvals → surface → ipc → routing → epicpanel → redirects → e2e) plus three parallel tracks:
  - tree: callsign/treemodel/rail → treeview/chatnodes → epicpanel/chatrail;
  - to-dos: todonorm/todomodel → todocard → todohide → activityline; changes;
  - arbiter: rules/verdict/launch/run/settings → arbitergate → attention → stall → notifyboot → landing.
- **S2:** deliverycheck → schema → verify → record → waive → runbar → panel → capture.
- **S3:** delivery → browserspike → contract → origin → session → host → dispatch → ipc → panel → origincard → camera → e2e.
- **S4:** delivery → gate → seam → rail → shots → capture.

## Final red team (5 critics, 73 findings, all applied as binding 'Final red-team fixes' sections in revision 2)
- **Blockers fixed:**
  - Callsign helpers and the `s1-chatrail` design now use only main-stamped callsigns.
  - Unordered bootstrap, preload and fake edits are serialized.
  - Skitarii approvals with no tool input are never arbitrated (no fail-open).
  - Browser durable storage uses a stable `folderStoreId`, not the per-run attachment key.
  - The CSP allows `dm-chat-image:`.
  - The legacy-terminal Magos is switched to the GUI and resumed after restart.
  - S4 merges main through a new `s4-sync` ticket.
  - S4's delivery check uses the PR merge commit, not ancestry.
  - The fake omp persona survives shim following.
- **Security hardening:**
  - The arbiter never sees truncated input (too large → escalate).
  - Control files (`.claude/`, `.git/`, `.omp/`, `.mcp.json`, CLAUDE.md…) are never arbitrated.
  - Windows path, UNC and encoded-command forms escalate.
  - Worktree roots count as inside the folder.
  - Unattributed prompts are never stamped Magos.
  - Claim bindings are verified against the claim before binding.
  - The arbiter runs with `--safe-mode` in an OS temp dir, and omp arbitration stays off until its MCP behaviour is observed.
  - Settings parse leniently and never silently loosen.
  - Page-initiated origin prompts cannot supersede agent prompts.
  - DNS and rebinding checks for private addresses.
  - An orchestrator cannot drop an unverified `delivery` by re-adopting a revision.
- **Transition logic:**
  - Delivery-check tickets are claimed only after the PR merge, a successful Deploy and the restart message.
  - Every sprint's exit criteria request PR delivery explicitly.
  - An unmerged desktop epic raises a blocker for the person instead of failing a ticket.
- **New tickets:** `s3-originattention` and `s4-sync`.

tickets.body:
## Outcome A checked-in protocol reference and golden JSONL transcripts that the two translators (`claudeparse`, `ompparse`) and the fake CLI (`fakecli`) are all built against. This is a bounded investigation that produces data and docs, not product code. ## Scope 1. Write `docs/reports/agent-chat-protocols.md`. For each protocol, give: - the launch argv; - every host→CLI line used: user turn, interrupt, and the permission/question answer; - every CLI→host event the GUI needs: init/ready, text and thinking deltas, the assistant message, tool start/update/end, subagent start/end with the parent link, the approval request, the question request, turn end or result, and error. Mark each field **observed** (with the source file and line) or **inferred**. Also record: - **Claude:** the `initialize` control handshake (required or not, with source); the full `control_request`/`control_response` envelopes including `request_id` for `can_use_tool`, `interrupt` and their responses; how AskUserQuestion reaches the host (a `can_use_tool` with `tool_name: "AskUserQuestion"`, per `87102b0c~1:src/main/agents/adapters/claudeApprovals.ts:31-34`) and its answer shape (`updatedInput` = the input plus `answers`); and how "allow for this chat" is encoded (`updatedPermissions` from the request's `permission_suggestions`, destination `session`). - **OMP:** the ready frame (including `maxFrameBytes`/`maxReassembledFrameBytes`); `rpc_chunk` framing in both directions; `set_subagent_subscription`; `follow_up` and `queue_update`; every `extension_ui_request` method, split into blocking and fire-and-forget; `cancel`; `secret`; and which tool-approval shape and which question shape appear under `--mode rpc-ui`. **`rpc-ui` is required:** OMP registers its ask tool only in that mode. 2. Write golden transcripts under `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/claude/` and `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/omp/`, one pair per scenario: - `.out.jsonl` is what the CLI prints. - `.in.jsonl` is what the host writes. **Scenarios:** - `text`: streamed reply. - `tool`: one tool call with its result. - `subagent`: a Task/subagent with a nested tool call. - `approval`: a tool permission request, allowed once. - `approval_chat`: allowed for this chat. - `question`: AskUserQuestion, or an omp ask answered. - `interrupt`: the turn is interrupted. - `error`: a failed turn. - `queued`: a second user turn sent mid-turn (omp: `follow_up` plus `queue_update`). - omp only: `chunked`, a tool result split into `rpc_chunk` lines. **Rules:** - The init/ready line (and, for omp, the `set_subagent_subscription` command and its response) lives only in `init.out.jsonl`/`init.in.jsonl`. Scenario files hold one turn's lines only. - Every id in a scenario contains the token `T1` (for example `msg_T1_a`, `toolu_T1_1`), so the fake CLI can renumber turns. - No timestamps; the fixtures are deterministic. - **Line endings:** add `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/**/*.jsonl text eol=lf` and `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/*.mjs text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes` (this edit is allowed despite Out of scope). Run `git add --renormalize .`, then confirm that `git ls-files --eol src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__` shows `i/lf w/lf`. Git for Windows' `core.autocrlf=true` would otherwise break the byte-for-byte tests. ## Sources (in order of trust) - **Claude:** - The removed adapter's real-stream handling: `git show 87102b0c~1:src/main/agents/adapters/claudeTranscript.ts`, `…/adapters/claudeApprovals.ts`, `…/adapters/claude.ts` (canUseTool ~:686-695) and `…/adapters/__mocks__/claudeSubagents.ts`. The old SDK spawned the same CLI with `--output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json --verbose --permission-prompt-tool stdio` (`docs/reports/agents-fixes-e2e.md:76`). - You may `npm pack @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@latest --pack-destination ` (registry.npmjs.org) and read `sdk.d.ts`. Record the exact version and integrity hash. Never add it as a dependency. Any field observed only in the SDK must quote the `sdk.d.ts` excerpt inline, so the reviewer can check it offline. - `claude --help` on the host lists the flags. - **Skitarii/OMP:** - The **OMP RPC fact sheet** appended to this ticket, extracted on 2026-11-20 from Ada's reader-side types, with source lines. - `docs/reports/omp-cli.md`: lines 98, 129 and 161 cover `--mode rpc|rpc-ui` and `--no-ui`. It was recorded on this same Windows host with omp 18.16.0. - If `omp` is installed on the host: `omp --version`, `omp --help`, and starting `omp --mode rpc-ui` with no prompt to capture the ready frame. Close stdin straight away and start no model turn. - If `/…/onebrief-harness` happens to be present, it may be read; otherwise the fact sheet is the source. - **Optional live observations, evidence only and never a gate:** 1. One `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --input-format stream-json --permission-prompt-tool stdio` run with the prompt `Reply with the single word OK`. Never pass `--bare`. 2. The same launch with the app-generated `--settings` file (`writeClaudeSettings` output) and the prompt `Write the word hi to /x.md`. Record whether a `can_use_tool` control_request arrives, whether it is denied, or whether the write just runs (this is the memory-guard check, lesson L5). If either is refused (no sign-in, no network), record the exact error and continue. ## Out of scope - Any code under `src/` other than the fixture files. - Installing anything. ## Decision output The report ends with a **Translator contract** table: for each CLI event, the `ChatItem` kind or delta it becomes (see Design §3). `claudeparse` and `ompparse` implement that table literally. ## Tests None: data and docs only. `fakecli` and both translators test against these fixtures. Every `.jsonl` line must parse as JSON; check with `node -e` over the files and paste the output into your evidence. ## Time limit (declared bounded-investigation exception) 40 minutes of active work. If one source is unreachable, mark its fields inferred and continue; do not block. ## Appendix: OMP RPC fact sheet # OMP (oh-my-pi / "Skitarii") RPC over JSONL stdio: protocol fact sheet Purpose: enough of the wire contract to write a host-side translator and a fake CLI without the source. Every fact is tagged OBSERVED (read in source or doc) or INFERRED (my reading, not stated). Citation prefixes: - `MGR` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/main/pi-rpc-manager.ts - `IPC` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/shared/ipc-contracts.ts - `HND` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/main/ipc/pi-handlers.ts - `APR` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/shared/tool-approval.ts - `FAKE` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/e2e/support/fake-a8s.mjs - `EUI` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/main/extension-ui-ipc.ts - `RTR` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/main/pi-event-router.ts - `WSM` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/main/workspace-manager.ts - `CHAT` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/renderer/src/chat/chat-state.ts - `SUB` = onebrief-harness/packages/desktop/src/shared/subagent-task.ts - `SEP` = onebrief-harness/packages/contracts/src/session-endpoint.ts - `RPCDOC` = onebrief-harness/docs/reference/rpc.md - `INT` = onebrief-harness/docs/reference/engineering-harness-internals.md - `OMPDOC` = DarkMechanicus/docs/reports/omp-cli.md (OMP 18.16.0, Windows 11) Version note: the desktop code targets OMP 18.16 to 18.20 (comments mention 18.16 `ask`, 18.18 forms, 18.20). OBSERVED MGR:66-68, INT docs. --- ## 1. Launch flags - `--mode ` picks the output mode; `text` is the default. OBSERVED OMPDOC:98. - `rpc` = JSON-lines commands, responses and events. `rpc-ui` = the same protocol **plus agent dialogs**. OBSERVED RPCDOC:10-13. - `rpc-ui` routes tool dialogs such as `ask` to the client. OBSERVED INT:1112-1113. OMP registers its `ask` tool only when the session has a host UI, i.e. in `rpc-ui`. OBSERVED MGR:54-55. With the ADA wrapper, `--tools ...,ask` under `--mode rpc` is a usage error. OBSERVED INT:1144-1146. - `--no-ui`: "With --mode rpc or rpc-ui: run extensions headless (rpc-ui tool UI remains enabled)". OBSERVED OMPDOC:129. - Other flags the desktop passes: `--profile `, `--provider

`, `--model `, `--thinking `, `--session ` or `--continue`, then caller args verbatim (e.g. `--tools a,b`). OBSERVED MGR:633-666; thinking values OBSERVED OMPDOC:147. - The argv order the desktop builds: `--mode --profile a8s [--provider P] [--model M] [--thinking L] [--session PATH | --continue] [extra args]`. `--thinking` is only added for a new session (no `--session`/`--continue`) and when the caller did not pass one. OBSERVED MGR:634-651. - Approval flags: `--approval-mode always-ask|always-ask-cached|write|yolo`, `--auto-approve` (skip approval prompts). OBSERVED OMPDOC:134-135. `--yolo` exists but is hidden from `--help`. OBSERVED OMPDOC:138. - Without `--mode rpc`, a non-TTY stdin is refused: "interactive mode requires a terminal ... use `--mode rpc`", exit 2. OBSERVED OMPDOC:160-161. - Version string: `omp --version` prints `omp/18.16.0`. Parse that, not `--help` (`omp v18.16.0`). OBSERVED OMPDOC:53-64. - No first prompt on the command line is needed in RPC: prompts arrive as `prompt` commands (section 3). INFERRED. (A TUI launch takes the first prompt as a positional arg. ## Outcome
The shared types every other ticket codes against exist and are tested.

## Source locations
- **New** `src/shared/agents/agentChat.ts`, following the style of `src/shared/agents/chatApi.ts`:
  - `AGENT_CHAT_CHANNELS`: `agentChat:start`, `agentChat:send`, `agentChat:interrupt`, `agentChat:answer`, `agentChat:setSurface`, `agentChat:snapshot`, and the push channel `agentChat:event`.
  - zod strict request schemas for each.
  - `AgentChatEvent`, the push union:
    - `{type:'item', folder, chatId, item: ChatItem}` (upsert by `item.id`)
    - `{type:'delta', folder, chatId, itemId, kind:'text'|'thinking', text}`
    - `{type:'status', folder, chatId, status: 'starting'|'idle'|'busy'|'exited'|'signed_out'|'failed', detail?}`
    - `{type:'pending', folder, chatId, prompt: PendingPrompt | null}`
    - `{type:'queued', folder, chatId, count}`
  - `PendingPrompt`: `{id, kind:'approval'|'question', title, detail, options:{id,label}[], tool?:{name, input}}`.
  - `AgentChatSnapshot`: `{items, status, pending, queued, surface}`.
  - `AgentChatApi`, the preload contract.
  - `GUI_PROTOCOL_KINDS = ['omp','claude'] as const`.
  - `agentChat:send` request = `z.strictObject({folder: string|null, chatId, text: z.string().min(1).max(20000)})`. Text only: no bytes, data URLs, paths or attachment ids cross IPC in v1.
  - `agentChat:answer` = `{folder, chatId, promptId, optionId, text?: max 20000}`.
  - `PendingPrompt.options[].id` is one of `allow_once | allow_chat | deny` for approvals, or the CLI's own option ids for questions.
- `src/shared/agents/chat.ts` `chatRecordSchema` (~l.55-107): add optional `epicId: string` and optional `surface: 'gui'|'terminal'`. Both must stay optional, so old `index.jsonl` lines still load.
- `src/main/agents/chatStore.ts`:
  - add `epicId` and `surface` to `NewChat` (l.45-46);
  - `ChatPatch` (l.51) allows `surface`, and allows `epicId` only when the record has none. Add a guard in the patch path that returns the record unchanged on an overwrite attempt.
- `src/main/agents/chatRecords.ts` `NewChatRequest` (l.47): add `epicId` and `surface`. The renderer's `chats:create` request schema must still not accept `epicId`.
- **Preload bridge:**
  - add `agentChat: AgentChatApi` to `DmApi` in `src/shared/desktop/api.ts` (l.251);
  - in `src/preload/index.ts`, add an `agentChat` object beside `chats` (l.57-80, `const dm: DmApi` at l.107). It makes one `ipcRenderer.invoke` per request channel, plus `onEvent(cb) → unsubscribe` on `agentChat:event`, validating each pushed event with the schema and dropping invalid ones.
  - The main handlers come later (`ipc`); until then the channels are simply unregistered.
- **Fakes:** new `src/renderer/src/__mocks__/idleAgentChat.ts` (pattern: `idleTerminals.ts`), assigned as `agentChat` in `FakeDm` (`src/renderer/src/__mocks__/fakeDm.ts:57`) and `FakeBackend` (`src/renderer/src/epic/__mocks__/fakeBackend.ts:112`).
- **Secret masker:** new `src/main/agentChat/secretMask.ts` exporting `maskAgentChatSecretsDeep(value)`. It applies `maskClaimTokensDeep` (`src/main/agents/claimTokenMask.ts`), then replaces the grant-token pattern. Export `GRANT_TOKEN` from `src/core/storedSecrets.ts:49-50` (`/dmg_[0-9a-f]{16,}/gi`) and reuse it there. **`maskClaimTokensDeep` alone does not mask `DM_SESSION_TOKEN`**: it only matches `at_`/`ka_` claim tokens.

## Out of scope
- Main-process handlers and behaviour (`ipc`, `sessions`).
- Renderer UI.

## Tests
- New `src/shared/agents/agentChat.test.ts`: each request schema accepts a valid input and rejects unknown keys; send rejects text over 20,000 characters and any extra field (such as `images` or `path`); `AgentChatEvent` round-trips.
- Extend `src/shared/agents/chat.test.ts`: a legacy record without `epicId`/`surface` parses; a record with both parses.
- Extend `src/main/agents/chatStore.test.ts`: `createChat` with `epicId` and `surface` persists both; a `surface` patch persists; an `epicId` patch on a record without one persists; overwriting an existing `epicId` is refused.
- Extend `src/preload/index.test.ts`: each `agentChat` method invokes its `agentChat:*` channel; `onEvent` drops an invalid pushed event.
- New `src/main/agentChat/secretMask.test.ts`: both a `dmg_…` grant token and an `at_…` claim token are masked inside nested objects and inside a longer string.

## Amendments from the Sprint 1 expansion (binding; they extend or replace the text above where stated)

### From the s1-todos drafter
In the `src/shared/agents/agentChat.ts` bullet list, after the `queued` event line, ADD the event `{type:'todos', folder, chatId, threadId: string | null, phases: AgentTodoPhase[]}` (null = the chat's own thread; an empty `phases` clears that thread's list; ephemeral, never persisted as a ChatItem). ADD after `PendingPrompt`: `agentTodoPhaseSchema` = `z.strictObject({name: z.string().max(200), tasks: z.array(agentTodoTaskSchema).max(100)})`, `agentTodoTaskSchema` = `z.strictObject({id: z.string().max(64).nullable(), content: z.string().min(1).max(500), activeForm: z.string().max(500).optional(), status: z.enum(['pending','in_progress','completed','blocked','abandoned']), blocker: z.string().max(500).optional()})`, phases array max 20, with exported types `AgentTodoPhase`/`AgentTodoTask`. CHANGE `AgentChatSnapshot` to `{items, status, pending, queued, surface, todos: {threadId: string | null, phases: AgentTodoPhase[]}[]}`. ADD `TODO_TOOL_NAMES = ['TodoWrite','TaskCreate','TaskUpdate','TaskList','TaskGet','todo'] as const` (the renderer hides these calls). Under Tests, ADD to `agentChat.test.ts`: a `todos` event round-trips; an unknown task status, a missing `content`, an extra key on a task, 101 tasks and 21 phases are each rejected; a snapshot without `todos` is rejected (main always sends it). ADD acceptance criterion: "`AgentChatEvent` includes the `todos` event, `AgentChatSnapshot` carries per-thread `todos`, and `agentTodoPhaseSchema` rejects unknown statuses, extra keys and over-limit lists (schema tests)". ADD to the preload bullet: pushed `todos` events go through the same event schema, so an invalid list is dropped.

### From the s1-approvals drafter
Add to the Source locations of the contract ticket:

- **New `src/shared/agents/callsign.ts`:**
  - `CALLSIGN_ROLES = ['Magos','Lexmechanic','Acolyte','Inquisitor','Servitor'] as const`;
  - `callsignSchema = z.strictObject({role: z.enum(CALLSIGN_ROLES), ticketKey: z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,12}-\d{1,9}$/).nullable(), ordinal: z.number().int().min(1).max(9999).nullable(), purpose: z.string().max(80).nullable(), ticketVerified: z.boolean()})`;
  - `type Callsign`;
  - `formatCallsign(c)`, which returns `Magos`, `Lexmechanic`, `<Role>:<KEY>` or `Servitor-<N>`.
  
  The parse and resolve logic comes later (`s1-callsign`).
- **`PendingPrompt`** (in `src/shared/agents/agentChat.ts`) gains:
  - `threadId: string | null`;
  - `callsign: Callsign | null`, set by main only;
  - `arbitration: {state: 'off'|'deciding'|'escalated', reason: string|null}`, with the reason at most 500 characters.
- **`src/shared/agents/chat.ts`:**
  - `approval_request` (l.~172) and `thread` (l.~226) gain an optional `callsign: callsignSchema`;
  - `approval_decision` (l.~189) gains an optional `decidedBy: z.enum(['person','magos'])` and an optional `reason: z.string().max(500)`;
  - all of them stay optional, so legacy lines parse unchanged.
- **The `agentChat:answer` request schema is unchanged.** The renderer can never send `decidedBy`, `reason` or `callsign`.

Add to Tests:
- `agentChat.test.ts`: a PendingPrompt with a callsign and arbitration round-trips, and `answer` with a `decidedBy` key is rejected.
- `chat.test.ts`: a legacy `approval_decision` without `decidedBy` parses; one with `decidedBy:'magos'` and a reason parses; `decidedBy:'robot'` is rejected.
- New `src/shared/agents/callsign.test.ts` stub: `formatCallsign` gives all four forms.

Add the acceptance criterion: "`PendingPrompt` carries threadId, callsign and arbitration; ChatItems accept an optional callsign and `decidedBy`/`reason` while legacy lines still parse; `agentChat:answer` rejects `decidedBy` (tests)".

tickets.body:
## Outcome
`src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/fakeAgentCli.mjs` acts like both CLIs, so the process runner, the session manager and the built-app e2e run with no network and no sign-in.

## Behaviour
- **Mode** comes from argv:
  - `--mode rpc-ui` or `--mode rpc` → omp protocol.
  - `-p` with `--output-format stream-json` → claude protocol.
  - `--version` → prints `2.1.329 (Claude Code)` and exits 0 (the app's agent probe, `src/main/desktop/agentProbe.ts:24`).
  - `auth status` → prints `{"loggedIn":true}` and exits 0, or `{"loggedIn":false}` and exits 1 when `FAKE_AGENT_SIGNED_OUT=1` (`src/main/desktop/agentAuth.ts:59,103-107`).
  - Anything else is **TUI mode** (the terminal launch from `terminalLaunchSpec.ts` `claudeLaunch`, which has no `-p`): print `fake-tui ready <sessionId>`, echo each stdin line, and exit 0 on stdin EOF (also on SIGHUP/SIGTERM where the platform delivers signals; Windows does not).
- **Logging:** every invocation, in every mode, first appends one line `{mode, pid: process.pid, argv, cwd, env: {DM_SESSION_TOKEN: present|absent}}` to the file named by `FAKE_AGENT_LOG` (pattern: `src/main/terminals/__fixtures__/agentFixture.mjs`). It does this before any other output, and never writes the token value.
- **File:** it starts with `#!/usr/bin/env node` and is committed executable (`git update-index --chmod=+x`).
- **Startup (protocol modes):** prints the golden `init.out.jsonl`. In omp mode it waits for `set_subagent_subscription` and answers it, as in `init.in/out`.
- **Per user line read on stdin:** picks a scenario by keyword in the prompt: `[tool]`, `[subagent]`, `[approval]`, `[approval_chat]`, `[question]`, `[error]`, `[slow]`, `[chunked]` (omp), `[leak]`. The default is `text`. It then replays that scenario's `.out.jsonl` from `proto`, with every `T1` replaced by `T<N>` for the Nth user turn, so turn 1 is byte-identical to the golden file and later turns have fresh ids.
  - For approval and question scenarios it stops after the request line and waits for the matching answer line before continuing.
  - `[slow]` waits 200 ms between lines, so interrupt and queued sends are testable. That is the only timer. A user line arriving during a turn is replayed after the turn, per the `queued` scenario.
  - `[leak]` prints the value of its own `DM_SESSION_TOKEN` env var inside a tool result and on stderr, to prove masking downstream.
- **Interrupt:** on an interrupt line (claude `control_request` `interrupt`, omp `abort`), replays the `interrupt` scenario tail.
- **Exit:** on stdin EOF exits 0; on `[crash]` exits 3 after printing one line to stderr.
- **Session files:** with `--session-id <uuid>`, writes `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl`, so `claudeSessionExists` (`src/main/terminals/claudeSession.ts:62`) sees a resumable session.

## Source locations
- New `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/fakeAgentCli.mjs`.
- Pattern to follow: `src/main/terminals/__fixtures__/agentFixture.mjs`.
- Golden inputs: `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/{claude,omp}/*.jsonl` (from `proto`).

## Tests
New `src/main/agentChat/fakeAgentCli.test.ts`, which spawns the fixture with `process.execPath`, piped stdio and a per-test temp dir:
- Each mode's turn-1 output for each scenario equals its golden file byte for byte.
- Two `text` turns produce disjoint ids.
- An `[approval]` turn blocks until the answer line is written.
- Interrupt during `[slow]` ends the turn with the interrupt tail.
- EOF exits 0.
- `--version`, `auth status` (signed in and signed out) and TUI mode behave as specified.
- Every mode writes one log line with its pid first.
- On every platform, TUI and protocol modes exit 0 on stdin EOF. The SIGTERM→0 assertion runs only when `process.platform !== 'win32'`, because Windows has no signal delivery (a platform fact, not a skip).
- Compare golden output after splitting on `/?
/`, and also assert the fixture files contain no ``.
- The log never contains the token value; `[leak]` does print it, which is intended.

## Amendments from the Sprint 1 expansion (binding; they extend or replace the text above where stated)

### From the s1-tree drafter
Add the keyword `[subagent_tree]` to the scenario keywords. It replays `subagent_tree.out.jsonl` (from `proto`) in both modes. The byte-for-byte turn-1 test covers it like every other scenario. Add one test: after a `[subagent_tree]` turn in claude mode, the fake's log line contains no `fixtureSecret`, because the log records only argv/cwd/env presence.

## Outcome
A pure translator, `src/main/agentChat/claudeProtocol.ts`, that turns one CLI stdout line plus its state into `{events: AgentChatEvent-payloads[], state}`, and encodes host commands into stdin lines. No I/O.

## Rules
- Implement the **Translator contract** table in `docs/reports/agent-chat-protocols.md` (from `proto`) literally.
- Output only `ChatItem`s from `src/shared/agents/chat.ts` (`chatItemSchema`: `user_message`, `assistant_text`, `tool_call`, `approval_request`, `approval_decision`, `error`, `turn_stopped`, `thread`, …), plus `delta`, `status`, `pending` and `queued` payloads from `src/shared/agents/agentChat.ts`.
- Subagent lines carry `parent_tool_use_id`. Map them to a `thread` item, as `87102b0c~1:src/main/agents/adapters/claudeTranscript.ts` did, so each worker subagent has its own thread id.
- A `control_request` `can_use_tool` whose `tool_name` is `AskUserQuestion` becomes a `PendingPrompt` of kind `question`, built from `input.questions`. Its answer is a `control_response` allow whose `updatedInput` is the held input plus the `answers` map, in the exact shape `proto` records.
- Every other `can_use_tool` becomes kind `approval`, with options `allow_once`, then `allow_chat` only when `permission_suggestions` is non-empty, then `deny`. `allow_chat` encodes as allow with `updatedPermissions` = the request's `permission_suggestions` with destination `session`.
- `updatedInput` is always the input main holds from the request, never renderer data.
- Map any other control subtype only if `proto` records it as observed.
- Encoders emit the full envelope: `{type:'control_response',response:{subtype:'success',request_id:<the request's id>,response:{…}}}`. User turns are `{type:'user',message:{role:'user',content}}`. Interrupt is a `control_request` `{subtype:'interrupt'}` with a fresh host `request_id`. If `proto` says `initialize` is required, the encoder exposes `initLines()`.
- Mask every string that will be stored or pushed with `maskAgentChatSecretsDeep` (`src/main/agentChat/secretMask.ts`, from `contract`) before returning it. Raw lines never leave this module.
- Unknown event types, and lines that are not valid JSON, become no event plus an incremented `skipped` counter. They never throw.
- Signal turn end as `status: idle`: the `result` line. A failed turn becomes an `error` item plus `status: idle`.

## Source locations
- New `src/main/agentChat/claudeProtocol.ts` and `src/main/agentChat/claudeProtocol.test.ts`.
- Fixtures: `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/claude/*.jsonl`.
- Prior art for state handling (Claude): `git show 87102b0c~1:src/main/agents/adapters/claudeTranscript.ts`.

## Tests
`claudeProtocol.test.ts` feeds `init` and each golden scenario `.out.jsonl` through the translator. For each scenario, assert the exact `ChatItem` list (kinds, ids, thread ids, tool status) and that every `delta` is later committed exactly once (no doubled text). Also assert:
- the encoder output equals each scenario's `.in.jsonl`;
- a planted `dmg_` grant token and an `at_` claim token in a tool result come out masked;
- garbage and unknown lines are skipped without throwing;
- fixtures are read by splitting on `/?
/`, and contain no ``.
- AskUserQuestion yields a `question` with its options, and its answer carries `answers`.
- `allow_chat` encodes `updatedPermissions` with destination `session`.
- Every response envelope carries the request's `request_id`.

## Amendments from the Sprint 1 expansion (binding; they extend or replace the text above where stated)

**Integration note (planner):** the thread-to-attempt binding event is `thread_claim` from `s1-threadclaim` (internal, never pushed or stored). Where an amendment says `binding`, read `thread_claim`. Every PendingPrompt is emitted with `callsign: null` and `arbitration: {state:'off', reason:null}`; main fills them in.

### From the s1-tree drafter
Add to Rules:
- **Forwarded subagent text:** with `--forward-subagent-text` (from `launch`), subagent assistant and user lines carry `parent_tool_use_id`. Their text becomes `assistant_text` items whose `threadId` is that thread's id; they are not mixed into the main thread.
- **Nested threads:** an `Agent`/`Task` tool_use inside a thread opens a nested `thread` item whose `threadId` is the enclosing thread's id.
- **Thread label:** `input.description`, else `input.subagent_type`, else `Subagent`. Strip control characters, clip to 120 characters, mask it, and never take it from `input.prompt`.
- **Timestamps:** a thread item that is rewritten when its state changes keeps its first `at`.

Tests: `subagent_tree` translates to the asserted items, with two worker threads under the main thread, the Inquisitor thread nested under worker 2, worker 1 `done`, and worker 2 `running`. No item, delta or label contains `fixtureSecret`.

Criterion 1: append "including forwarded subagent text and the nested `subagent_tree` threads".

### From the s1-todos drafter
ADD to Rules: (1) **File paths kept whole:** when summarizing a `tool_call` input, keep `file_path`, `notebook_path` and `path` verbatim (masked, up to 4,096 characters) for every tool, so the Changes card can list them (renderer `SUMMARY_KEYS` already reads `file_path`, `src/renderer/src/agents/chatViewModel.ts:43`). (2) **To-dos:** on a **successful** tool_result (not `is_error`) for a held `TodoWrite` tool_use, emit `{type:'todos', threadId, phases: todoWritePhases(input)}` (from `s1-todonorm`); for `TaskCreate`, call `taskCreateStarted` on the tool_use and `taskCreateResult` on its successful result; for `TaskUpdate`, call `taskUpdate` on its successful result; after each change emit `todos` with `taskPhases(list)`. Keep one `TaskList` and one TodoWrite list per thread in translator state; `threadId` is the thread mapped from `parent_tool_use_id`, else null. A failed todo call emits no `todos` event and stays a failed `tool_call`. A `null` (rejected) list emits nothing and increments `skipped`. The todo calls themselves still become ordinary `tool_call` items. ADD to Tests: the `todo`, `tasks`, `todo_fail` and `edit` fixtures: `todo` emits two main-thread `todos` events and one for the subagent thread; `tasks` ends with task 1 completed and task 2 pending, the unknown id `99` changes nothing; `todo_fail` emits no `todos`; `edit` tool_calls carry the absolute `file_path`/`notebook_path` unchanged. ADD acceptance criterion: "Successful TodoWrite and TaskCreate/TaskUpdate calls emit per-thread `todos` events, failed ones emit none, and file-tool `tool_call` inputs keep `file_path`/`notebook_path` verbatim (fixture tests)". ADD `s1-todonorm` to requires.

### From the s1-approvals drafter
Add under Rules:

- **Thread of a request.** A `can_use_tool` raised by a subagent carries that thread's id as `PendingPrompt.threadId` and as the `approval_request` item's `threadId`. The thread is found by the subagent's agent id when the request gives one, otherwise by the `tool_use_id` of a call made in a message whose `parent_tool_use_id` names the thread's spawn. Prior art: `threadOfRequest`, `git show 87102b0c~1:src/main/agents/adapters/claudeTranscript.ts:229-233`.
- **No match:** the main thread, with `threadId: null`.
- **Defaults:** every emitted PendingPrompt has `callsign: null` and `arbitration: {state:'off', reason:null}`; main fills them in.

Add to Tests: in the `subagent` scenario, a request raised inside the thread carries its thread id, and a main-thread request carries null.

## Final red-team fixes (binding; where a fix contradicts text above, the fix wins)

**Fix 21 [major]** An approval that cannot be tied to a thread is stamped with the main-thread callsign. In a Magos chat a worker's request is then shown, notified and sent to the arbiter as `Magos`, the most trusted name, with no ticket. For OMP this applies to every worker approval.

**Required change:** Add a translator field `PendingPrompt.attributed: boolean`, true only when the thread is known, or when the request is provably from the main turn because no subagent is running. In s1-callsignresolve, an unattributed prompt in a chat with running threads gets callsign null and is displayed as 'An agent in <chat>'. The arbiter request uses requester 'unknown'. Test: an OMP select approval while a subagent runs is not stamped Magos.

## Outcome
A pure translator, `src/main/agentChat/ompProtocol.ts`, that turns one CLI stdout line plus its state into `{events: AgentChatEvent-payloads[], state}`, and encodes host commands into stdin lines. No I/O.

## Rules
- Implement the **Translator contract** table in `docs/reports/agent-chat-protocols.md` (from `proto`) literally.
- Output only `ChatItem`s from `src/shared/agents/chat.ts` (`chatItemSchema`: `user_message`, `assistant_text`, `tool_call`, `approval_request`, `approval_decision`, `error`, `turn_stopped`, `thread`, …), plus `delta`, `status`, `pending` and `queued` payloads from `src/shared/agents/agentChat.ts`.
- `message_update.assistantMessageEvent` deltas (`text_delta`, `thinking_delta`, `toolcall_*`) become `delta` events and are committed into `assistant_text`/`tool_call` items on `message_end`/`turn_end`. `tool_execution_start/update/end` update the tool item. `subagent_lifecycle`/`subagent_progress` become `thread` items.
- `initLines(readyFrame)` returns the post-ready commands from `init.in.jsonl`: `negotiate_protocol` (when v2 is supported), `set_ask_dialog {enabled:true}`, `set_subagent_subscription {level:'progress'}`, `set_event_filter {events:null, messageUpdates:'delta'}`. They are sent once, before the first `prompt`. A `prompt` finishes on its `prompt_result`, not on its `response`.
- **Blocking `extension_ui_request` methods** (`select`, `confirm`, `input`, `editor`, `ask`, `form`) each become a `PendingPrompt`: a `select` is a tool approval when its last option is exactly `Deny` and an earlier option is exactly `Approve` or `Approve Once` (fact sheet §Tool approval): the once option → `allow_once`, the first option ending `for this session` → `allow_chat`, `Deny` → `deny`; other grant options are not offered, and the answer is `{value:<the original option string>}` held in translator state. Any other `select`, and every `confirm`, → `question` with its options; `input`/`editor`/`ask`/`form` → `question` with free text. Text from a `secret: true` input is never stored or echoed. Any unknown blocking method becomes a `question` showing its raw title; it is never dropped, because a dropped prompt hangs the turn.
- `cancel` with a target id clears that pending prompt (`pending: null`).
- **Fire-and-forget methods** (`notify`, `setStatus`, `setWidget`, `setTitle`, `setWorkingMessage`, `set_editor_text`, `open_url`) are never answered, never shown as prompts, and never open anything. The app's own Skitarii extension emits several of them.
- **Sends:** a user turn sent while a turn is in flight encodes as `follow_up`, not `prompt`. `queue_update` becomes `queued` with `followUp.length + steering.length`.
- **Ids:** every command carries an id. A `{type:'response',success:false}` for an id becomes an `error` item.
- **`rpc_chunk`:** lines are reassembled before translation (canonical base64, in-order indexes, total under the advertised `maxReassembledFrameBytes`, else one `error` item). Outbound lines over `maxFrameBytes` are chunked.
- The encoder writes `prompt`, `follow_up`, `abort` and `extension_ui_response`. This is a reimplementation from the protocol report; do not copy Ada's code.
- Mask every string that will be stored or pushed with `maskAgentChatSecretsDeep` (`src/main/agentChat/secretMask.ts`, from `contract`) before returning it. Raw lines never leave this module.
- Unknown event types, and lines that are not valid JSON, become no event plus an incremented `skipped` counter. They never throw.
- Signal turn end as `status: idle`: `prompt_result` (it arrives after `agent_end`). A failed turn becomes an `error` item plus `status: idle`.

## Source locations
- New `src/main/agentChat/ompProtocol.ts` and `src/main/agentChat/ompProtocol.test.ts`.
- Fixtures: `src/main/agentChat/__fixtures__/omp/*.jsonl`.
- Prior art for state handling (Claude): `git show 87102b0c~1:src/main/agents/adapters/claudeTranscript.ts`.

## Tests
`ompProtocol.test.ts` feeds `init` and each golden scenario `.out.jsonl` through the translator. For each scenario, assert the exact `ChatItem` list (kinds, ids, thread ids, tool status) and that every `delta` is later committed exactly once (no doubled text). Also assert:
- the encoder output equals each scenario's `.in.jsonl`;
- a planted `dmg_` grant token and an `at_` claim token in a tool result come out masked;
- garbage and unknown lines are skipped without throwing;
- fixtures are read by splitting on `/?
/`, and contain no ``.
- Each blocking method yields a PendingPrompt.
- Each fire-and-forget method yields no prompt and no response line.
- `cancel` clears the matching prompt.
- `chunked` reassembles into one tool output.
- A send during a turn encodes as `follow_up`.

## Amendments from the Sprint 1 expansion (binding; they extend or replace the text above where stated)

**Integration note (planner):** the thread-to-attempt binding event is `thread_claim` from `s1-threadclaim` (internal, never pushed or stored). Every PendingPrompt is emitted with `callsign: null` and `arbitration: {state:'off', reason:null}`.

### From the s1-tree drafter
Add to Rules:
- **Threads:** `subagent_lifecycle`/`subagent_progress` create and update one `thread` item per subagent id. Its label is the payload `description`, else `agent`, else `Subagent`, with control characters stripped, clipped to 120 characters and masked. The label is never taken from `task`.
- **Nesting:** a nested subagent nests (`threadId` = parent thread) only through a parent field that `proto` recorded as observed; otherwise it sits under the main thread.
- **Timestamps:** a rewritten thread item keeps its first `at`.

Tests: `subagent_tree` translates to the asserted thread items, and no output contains `fixtureSecret`.

### From the s1-todos drafter
ADD to Rules: (1) **File paths kept whole:** keep `file_path`, `path` and `notebook_path` verbatim (masked, up to 4,096 characters) in `tool_call` inputs. (2) **To-dos:** `tool_execution_end` with `toolName === 'todo'` and `isError: false` emits `{type:'todos', threadId, phases: ompTodoPhases(result.details.phases)}` (from `s1-todonorm`); `threadId` is the subagent thread when the event belongs to one, else null. `todo_auto_clear` emits `todos` with `phases: []` for thread null. `isError: true` emits nothing. (3) `initLines` also sends `get_state` after `set_event_filter`; its response's `data.todoPhases` emits a main-thread `todos` event (empty when `[]`). ADD to Tests: the `todo` fixture emits phases with the blocked task's blocker and the abandoned task; `todo_fail` emits none; `todo_clear` emits an empty list; `init_resume` emits the stored phases; `edit` tool_calls keep their path; the encoder output equals the updated `init.in.jsonl` including `get_state`. ## Outcome
- A pure `agentChatLaunch(input)` that returns `{file, args, cwd, env, sessionId, resumed, protocol:'omp'|'claude'}` for a GUI chat.
- A pure `pickChatAgent(agents, auth)` in `src/shared/agents/pickChatAgent.ts`, so the renderer can use it too. It chooses the agent when **none is named**: the renderer's New chat default, and `chats:startPlanner`.

## Rules
- **`pickChatAgent`:**
  - Skitarii/`omp` if it is installed and its auth is `signed_in`.
  - Otherwise the first `signed_in` agent whose kind is in `GUI_PROTOCOL_KINDS` (claude).
  - Otherwise the first `signed_in` agent of any kind, with `surface: 'terminal'` (no GUI protocol).
  - Otherwise null, so the caller shows the existing sign-in path.
  - It returns `{agentId, surface}`.
- **claude argv:** `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio --append-system-prompt-file <instructions> [--settings <chat settings>] [--model m] (--session-id|--resume) <uuid>`. Never `--bare`. Never `--no-session-persistence`. Never `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

tickets.body:
## Outcome
`src/main/agentChat/agentProcess.ts` exports `startAgentProcess(spec, spawn = child_process.spawn)`. It returns `{write(line), onLine(cb), onStderr(cb), onExit(cb), stop(): Promise<void>, pid}`.

## Rules
- **Spawn:** piped stdio, `detached: true` on POSIX so the child leads its process group (see `startsOwnGroup` usage in `src/main/agents/processTree.ts`), `windowsHide`.
- **Framing:** split stdout on LF and strip CR. Buffer a partial line until the next chunk; flush it on `end`. Lines over 8 MiB are dropped with one stderr-tail note.
- **Diagnostics:** keep the last 64 KiB of stderr.
- **Writes:** `write` appends `\n`. EPIPE after exit is swallowed and reported as exited, never thrown.
- **Stop:** `stop()` ends stdin, then calls `killProcessTree` (`processTree.ts:247`) after 3 s if the child is still alive. It resolves when the child has exited, bounded at 5 s, so quit disposal (`src/main/quitDisposal.ts`) can finish.

## Tests
New `src/main/agentChat/agentProcess.test.ts`, using `fakeAgentCli.mjs` from `fakecli`:
- Lines split across chunks arrive whole.
- A trailing line without LF is flushed on exit.
- `stop()` resolves within 5 s, and `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws ESRCH for both the child pid and the fake's own logged pid. Never use ps or pgrep.
- `write` after exit does not throw.
- `[crash]` reports exit code 3 and the stderr tail.

Spawn the fake as `{file: process.execPath, args: [FAKE_CLI, ...]}`, which works on Windows. Use fake timers only for the 3 s escalation, with an injected `spawn` stub that ignores stdin EOF.

## Outcome
`src/main/agentChat/agentChatSessions.ts` exports `createAgentChatSessions(deps)`. It returns `{start(ref, {firstMessage?}), snapshot(ref), stop(ref), deleteChat(ref), isLive(ref), busy(), dispose()}`. This ticket covers start, lines, exit and dispose only:
- send, interrupt and lazy start are added by `sessionsend`;
- answer by `approvals`;
- `setSurface` by `surface`.

## Start pipeline
The order mirrors `runStart` in `src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts:896`:
1. `checkAuth` (deps; for claude that is `auth status`); `signed_out` → push `status: signed_out` and stop.
2. Write the start files (`writeTerminalFiles`, `writeClaudeSettings` for claude, `writeOmpFiles` for omp).
3. `resolveLaunchFolder` re-check.
4. Issue the grant (`issueChatCli` for a folder chat, `issueReachCli` for a project-less chat, from `src/main/agents/chatGrants.ts`).
5. `agentChatLaunch` (from `launch`), then record `grantIds` and `sessionId` on the chat.
6. `startAgentProcess` (from `process`), then write the translator's `initLines`.
7. `bindGrants`.
8. The first user turn is `firstMessage` (routing kickoffs), or else `chat.firstPrompt` when `kickoffSent` is false (the New chat popup). Write it, append and push it as a `user_message`, then set `kickoffSent`, and `firstPromptDelivery: 'submitted'` when it was the first prompt, as `terminalSessions.ts:593-624` does.

The renewal and folder watch of `watchLive` (hourly grant renew, 60 s folder re-check, `keepAwake`) apply unchanged.

## Lines
Each stdout line goes to the translator for the chat's protocol (`claudeProtocol`/`ompProtocol`). Items are appended to the store (`appendItems`) and pushed with `push(event)`; deltas are pushed only. **Every pushed or stored value**, including `status.detail` and the stderr tail, passes `maskAgentChatSecretsDeep`.

## Exit
- Revoke the grant on every exit path (see `revokeChatGrant`).
- Push `status: exited` or `failed`, with the masked stderr tail clipped to 2 KiB.
- `pauseIfSignedOut` logic applies to orchestrator chats (terminalSessions l.776).

## Rules
- No idle stop. Detaching never stops the process.
- One owner per chat: `start` refuses with `{code:'busy_elsewhere'}` when `deps.terminalLive(ref)` is true.

## Source locations
- New `src/main/agentChat/agentChatSessions.ts`, plus a test rig `src/main/agentChat/__mocks__/agentChatRig.ts` modelled on `src/main/terminals/__mocks__/terminalSessionsRig.ts`.
- The rig runs the fake on **every** platform. It sets `platform: process.platform`, never an injected platform that differs from the host's, and gives the agent an executable the launch accepts:
  - on win32, a generated `fake-claude.cmd`, a real npm-style shim that both cmd.exe and `SHIM_TARGET` accept, with CRLF line endings: `@ECHO off` / `SETLOCAL` / `SET dp0=%~dp0` / `node "%dp0%\fake-claude.js" %*`. `node` must resolve from `PATH`, so the isolated env keeps `PATH`. Next to it, `fake-claude.js` runs `import(require('node:url').pathToFileURL(<abs path of fakeAgentCli.mjs>).href)`; a bare `C:\…` path makes `import()` fail with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME;
  - on POSIX, the executable `.mjs` itself.
  
  The generator lives in new `src/main/agentChat/__mocks__/fakeAgentShim.ts`.
- Reuse `src/main/agents/chatGrants.ts`, `src/main/agents/launchFolder.ts`, `src/main/terminals/terminalFiles.ts` and `src/main/terminals/keepAwake.ts`.

## Tests
New `src/main/agentChat/agentChatSessions.test.ts`, with the fake CLI as the agent executable, a temp `userData`, and fake timers only for renew and the folder watch:
- Start → `text` turn → items persisted and pushed in order; the kickoff is delivered once and `kickoffSent` is set.
- Signed-out stops before spawning.
- A moved folder refuses to start.
- The grant is revoked on exit and on `dispose()`.
- `dispose()` resolves within 5 s and leaves the child's pid dead (`process.kill(pid,0)` throws).
- Start is refused while `terminalLive` is true.
- A test named **`never stores or pushes the session token`**: with a real-looking `dmg_` token in the grant env, it runs a `[leak]` turn and then a `[crash]`. Before teardown it reads every line of every file under the temp userData, plus every recorded push (including `status.detail`), and asserts that none contains the token value.

The in-memory lists are reset when a new process starts for the chat (omp refills them from `get_state`), and kept after exit so a reattach still sees the last list. ## Outcome
`agentChatSessions` gains `send(ref, {text})` and `interrupt(ref)`.

## Rules
- **Send to an idle chat:** writes a user turn with the translator's encoder.
- **Send while a turn is in flight:**
